extracted.intended_audience: journalists, editors, journalism students, and news organizations
extracted.subtask_description: Principles and actionable standards journalists should follow when gathering, reporting, and presenting news to serve the public interest while maintaining integrity and minimizing harm. Covers truthfulness, privacy, independence, accountability, and professional conduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preamble / Purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: Members of the Society of Professional Journalists believe that public enlightenment is the forerunner of justice and the foundation of democracy. The duty of the journalist is to further those ends by seeking truth and providing a fair and comprehensive account of events and issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The code is adopted to declare the Society's principles and standards of practice; it is intended as a resource for ethical decision-making, not as legally enforceable rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seek Truth and Report It — honesty, fairness and courage
rubrics_metrics.description: Journalists should be honest, fair and courageous in gathering, reporting and interpreting information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an overarching principle that frames the more specific practices listed below.

rubrics_metrics.name: Test accuracy and avoid error
rubrics_metrics.description: Test the accuracy of information from all sources and exercise care to avoid inadvertent error. Deliberate distortion is never permissible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use verification practices for all claims; treating mistakes as unacceptable except when corrected promptly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seek responses from subjects
rubrics_metrics.description: Diligently seek out subjects of news stories to give them the opportunity to respond to allegations of wrongdoing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Actively contact and include subject responses when reporting allegations to ensure fairness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify sources whenever feasible
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify sources whenever feasible. The public is entitled to as much information as possible on sources' reliability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide sufficient attribution and context about source credibility to allow readers to evaluate information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Question motives before granting anonymity
rubrics_metrics.description: Always question sources' motives before promising anonymity. Clarify conditions attached to any promise made in exchange for information. Keep promises.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be cautious with anonymous sources, document reasons for anonymity, and honor agreed conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid misrepresentation in headlines and promotions
rubrics_metrics.description: Make certain that headlines, news teases and promotional material, photos, video, audio, graphics, sound bites and quotations do not misrepresent. They should not oversimplify or highlight incidents out of context.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure packaging and summaries accurately reflect story content; avoid sensational or misleading framing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not distort photos or video
rubrics_metrics.description: Never distort the content of news photos or video. Image enhancement for technical clarity is always permissible. Label montages and photo illustrations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technical adjustments that clarify are allowed; any montage or illustration must be labeled to prevent deception.

rubrics_metrics.name: Label re-enactments
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid misleading re-enactments or staged news events. If re-enactment is necessary to tell a story, label it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clearly disclose staged or recreated elements so audiences are not misled about authenticity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use undercover methods only when necessary
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid undercover or other surreptitious methods of gathering information except when traditional open methods will not yield information vital to the public. Use of such methods should be explained as part of the story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reserve covert techniques for cases of clear public interest and always disclose rationale and methods to readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Never plagiarize
rubrics_metrics.description: Never plagiarize.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Always attribute and avoid representing others' work or words as one's own.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tell diverse stories boldly
rubrics_metrics.description: Tell the story of the diversity and magnitude of the human experience boldly, even when it is unpopular to do so.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pursue underrepresented perspectives and cover broad human experiences rather than only mainstream or popular angles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examine cultural values and avoid imposing them
rubrics_metrics.description: Examine their own cultural values and avoid imposing those values on others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practice self-awareness and cultural sensitivity in framing stories and interpreting behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid stereotyping
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid stereotyping by race, gender, age, religion, ethnicity, geography, sexual orientation, disability, physical appearance or social status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use nuanced reporting to prevent reducing people to simplistic or prejudiced portrayals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support open exchange of views
rubrics_metrics.description: Support the open exchange of views, even views they find repugnant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give space to diverse opinions and uphold free expression while providing context and fact-checking as needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Give voice to the voiceless
rubrics_metrics.description: Give voice to the voiceless; official and unofficial sources of information can be equally valid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include marginalized or less-heard sources and balance them with verification and context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish advocacy from reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Distinguish between advocacy and news reporting. Analysis and commentary should be labeled and not misrepresent fact or context.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Label opinion, analysis and commentary clearly so audiences understand the difference from factual reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish news from advertising
rubrics_metrics.description: Distinguish news from advertising and shun hybrids that blur the lines between the two.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid native ads or sponsored content that could be mistaken for independent reporting; disclose commercial relationships.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure public business is open
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize a special obligation to ensure that the public's business is conducted in the open and that government records are open to inspection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize transparency in reporting on government and public institutions and use FOI tools where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimize Harm — treat people with respect
rubrics_metrics.description: Ethical journalists treat sources, subjects and colleagues as human beings deserving of respect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This principle underlies the more specific guidance on sensitivity, privacy and taste.

rubrics_metrics.name: Show compassion for those adversely affected
rubrics_metrics.description: Show compassion for those who may be affected adversely by news coverage. Use special sensitivity when dealing with children and inexperienced sources or subjects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be considerate in questioning, depiction and follow-up with vulnerable individuals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be sensitive in tragedy coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: Be sensitive when seeking or using interviews or photographs of those affected by tragedy or grief.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid exploitative imagery or intrusive approaches; respect mourning and trauma.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognize reporting may cause harm
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize that gathering and reporting information may cause harm or discomfort. Pursuit of the news is not a license for arrogance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Weigh public interest against potential harm and act with humility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respect privacy of private people
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize that private people have a greater right to control information about themselves than do public officials and others who seek power, influence or attention. Only an overriding public need can justify intrusion into anyone's privacy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Differentiate public figures from private individuals and require strong public-interest justification before intruding into private lives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Show good taste; avoid lurid pandering
rubrics_metrics.description: Show good taste. Avoid pandering to lurid curiosity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refrain from sensationalism that exploits suffering or shock value for attention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be cautious identifying juvenile suspects or sex-crime victims
rubrics_metrics.description: Be cautious about identifying juvenile suspects or victims of sex crimes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protect identities when appropriate to avoid further harm or legal consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be judicious about naming suspects before charges
rubrics_metrics.description: Be judicious about naming criminal suspects before the formal filing of charges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider presumption of innocence and potential harm of premature identification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance fair trial rights with public's right to know
rubrics_metrics.description: Balance a criminal suspect's fair trial rights with the public's right to be informed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coordinate with legal considerations and avoid reporting that could jeopardize due process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Act Independently — avoid obligations to interests
rubrics_metrics.description: Journalists should be free of obligation to any interest other than the public's right to know.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Independence is foundational; see the specific prohibitions and disclosure duties below.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid conflicts of interest
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid conflicts of interest, real or perceived.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recuse or disclose when personal, financial or other ties could influence coverage or appear to do so.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remain free of compromising associations
rubrics_metrics.description: Remain free of associations and activities that may compromise integrity or damage credibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider outside activities (political, organizational) that could undermine impartiality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refuse gifts and shun compromising employment
rubrics_metrics.description: Refuse gifts, favors, fees, free travel and special treatment, and shun secondary employment, political involvement, public office and service in community organizations if they compromise journalistic integrity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set strict boundaries on acceptance of benefits and outside roles that might influence reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclose unavoidable conflicts
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclose unavoidable conflicts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When conflicts cannot be avoided, be transparent with audiences about them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hold power accountable
rubrics_metrics.description: Be vigilant and courageous about holding those with power accountable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize watchdog reporting and resist pressures that would shield powerful actors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deny favored treatment to advertisers and special interests
rubrics_metrics.description: Deny favored treatment to advertisers and special interests and resist their pressure to influence news coverage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain editorial independence from commercial relationships and report any influence attempts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid paying for information or bidding for news
rubrics_metrics.description: Be wary of sources offering information for favors or money; avoid bidding for news.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not create market incentives for sources to manufacture or sell stories; preserve editorial judgment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be Accountable — openness to public and colleagues
rubrics_metrics.description: Journalists are accountable to their readers, listeners, viewers and each other.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accountability involves transparency, correction, and internal and external critique.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarify coverage and invite dialogue
rubrics_metrics.description: Clarify and explain news coverage and invite dialogue with the public over journalistic conduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Engage audiences, explain decisions and be open to questions about reporting choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encourage public grievances
rubrics_metrics.description: Encourage the public to voice grievances against the news media.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide accessible ways for complaints and feedback and take them seriously.

rubrics_metrics.name: Admit mistakes and correct promptly
rubrics_metrics.description: Admit mistakes and correct them promptly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Corrections should be visible, timely, and sincere to maintain trust.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expose unethical practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Expose unethical practices of journalists and the news media.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be willing to investigate and call out wrongdoing within the profession.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hold self to same standards as others
rubrics_metrics.description: Abide by the same high standards to which they hold others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply ethical rules consistently to one's own work and that of colleagues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Code is voluntary and non-enforceable
rubrics_metrics.description: The SPJ Code of Ethics is voluntarily embraced by thousands of journalists... The code is intended not as a set of 'rules' but as a resource for ethical decision-making. It is not — nor can it be under the First Amendment — legally enforceable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the code as guidance for decisions rather than a set of legally binding obligations; adapt principles to context.
